test_title: PYST 60: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An object is placed 10 cm from a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. Which statement about the image is correct?

options.text: Image is real, inverted and smaller than the object.
Image is virtual, erect and larger than the object.
Image is virtual, erect and smaller than the object.
Image is real, inverted and larger than the object.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Image is virtual, erect and smaller than the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is also known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges the light rays that pass through it. It is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• For a **concave lens**, the **focal length (f)** is always taken as **negative**. In this case, **f = -15 cm**.
 
• The **object distance (u)** is always **negative** according to the sign convention. Here, **u = -10 cm**.
 
• Using the **Lens Formula**, **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**, where **v** is the image distance:
 
 
• **1/v = 1/f + 1/u**
 
• **1/v = 1/(-15) + 1/(-10)**
 
• **1/v = -1/15 - 1/10**
 
• **1/v = (-2 - 3) / 30 = -5/30 = -1/6**
 
• Therefore, **v = -6 cm**.
 
 
 
• The negative sign of **v** indicates that the image is **virtual** and formed on the **same side** as the object. All virtual images formed by a single lens are **erect**.
 
• The **magnification (m)** is calculated as **m = v/u**. Substituting the values: **m = -6 / -10 = 0.6**. Since the magnitude of **m** is less than **1**, the image is **smaller than the object** (diminished).
 
• Statement 1: Image is real, inverted and smaller than the object. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2: Image is virtual, erect and larger than the object. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3: Image is virtual, erect and smaller than the object. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 4: Image is real, inverted and larger than the object. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Images in Concave Lenses:**
 
 
• Regardless of the position of the **object**, a **concave lens** always produces a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image.
 
• The image is always formed between the **optical center** and the **principal focus (F1)** on the same side as the object.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):**
 
 
• If **m** is **positive**, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
• If **m** is **negative**, the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• If **|m| 1**, the image is **enlarged**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention (New Cartesian):**
 
 
• The **optical center (O)** is taken as the origin.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are **positive**; opposite to it are **negative**.
 
• Height measured upwards and perpendicular to the **principal axis** is **positive**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power of a Lens:** The power (P) is the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (**P = 1/f**). For a **concave lens**, since **f** is negative, the **power** is also **negative**.
 
• **Applications of Concave Lenses:**
 
 
• Used in **spectacles** to correct **myopia** (short-sightedness).
 
• Used in **peepholes** of house doors to provide a wide-angle view of people outside.
 
• Used in **flashlights** to spread the light beam over a wider area.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Convex Lenses:** Unlike concave lenses, **convex lenses** can form both **real** and **virtual** images, which can be **enlarged, diminished, or same-sized** depending on the object's distance from the lens.
